summary: POTONG is a Thai-Chinese tasting-menu restaurant in a five-storey, century-old family herbal-medicine shophouse in Chinatown. The meal combines the chef’s family heritage, historic rooms and a multi-course menu; the current menu is listed at ฿6,700++ per guest.
whyGo: A distinctive way to experience contemporary Thai-Chinese cooking alongside the story and interiors of a historic Yaowarat building.
MICHELIN highlights dishes such as the signature 14-day aged duck and creative reinterpretations of familiar Thai-Chinese flavours.
bestFor: A special-occasion dinner for diners who enjoy structured tasting menus and can plan ahead.
Food-minded travelers who want a Chinatown meal with a strong sense of place.
skipIf: You want a casual, quick or lower-cost meal, or prefer to choose à la carte.
You need a vegetarian menu or have significant allergies or dietary restrictions; confirm suitability with the restaurant before paying a deposit.
duration: Allow about 2.5–3 hours for the tasting menu. The restaurant holds a three-hour dining window and asks guests to arrive promptly.
cost: The official reservation page lists the tasting menu at ฿6,700++ per person, excluding 10% service charge and 7% VAT (about ฿7,839). It also lists water at ฿220++ per guest; if charged, that brings the estimate to about ฿8,096 before pairings or other drinks. Recheck the menu when booking.
hours: MICHELIN lists 15:30–23:00 Monday, Tuesday and Thursday–Sunday, closed Wednesday. The restaurant offers dinner seatings from 15:30 through 20:30; check the booking calendar for the exact December date and holiday changes.
bestTime: Book ahead for December and choose a seating that leaves time to enjoy the full course. Earlier seatings can make it easier to explore Yaowarat before or after dinner.
gettingThere: At 422 Vanich 1 Road, Samphanthawong. The restaurant recommends Bangkok MRT Blue Line to Wat Mangkon (BL29), Exit 1, then a roughly five-minute walk via Plaeng Nam Road and Yaowa Phanit Road. The lane is narrow for large vehicles. Drivers can use nearby Wat Chaiyaphum Karam parking and walk about three minutes, or park at Wat Pathumkongka and call for the restaurant shuttle; parking is listed at ฿40/hour.
booking: Reserve through the official website’s online booking link (Chope). The restaurant requires a ฿1,000-per-person deposit, applied to the final bill; it is non-refundable, though changes are allowed up to 48 hours before the booking. Tell the restaurant about food requirements at least seven days ahead; it says it cannot accommodate all allergies. Check availability, December holiday service, current price and menu before confirming.
accessibility: The building has a lift, but the restaurant warns that the stairs are steep and recommends avoiding high heels. It does not publish details on step-free entry, lift dimensions, accessible toilets or wheelchair suitability. Contact the restaurant at +66 82 979 3950 before booking to discuss access needs.
practicalTips: Wear smart casual clothing; men are asked to wear long trousers and covered shoes. The restaurant recommends avoiding high heels because of the stairs.
Guests must be at least 9 and children receive the same tasting menu as adults.
Arrive on time: the restaurant says a delay beyond 30 minutes may require adjustments to the experience.
The restaurant serves one tasting menu; seasonal ingredients may change individual dishes.
decemberNotes: The current official menu and timetable are a useful planning baseline for December 2026, but no December holiday schedule or date-specific menu has been published in the sources checked. Confirm the exact date and current booking terms directly; the restaurant is closed Wednesdays.
uncertainties: December 2026 holiday openings, availability, menu and pricing may change.
Accessibility details beyond the existence of a lift are not published; step-free access and wheelchair suitability remain unverified.
The restaurant says it cannot accommodate all allergies, so suitability for a particular diet must be confirmed directly.
